audit.why: 47.32% over 746 games; HARD / 6-10 difficulty matches. Sett wins the early stat-check brawl and Fiora reclaims it at two items — the prose already says this correctly.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart handed Levels 4-5 and First item to Fiora and called Levels 1, 2 and 6 'Skill', while the packet chart reads Sett/Sett/Skill/Sett/Sett/Sett/Fiora and every matching whys[] entry says Sett wins those rows.
audit.why: whys[0] 'out-grit your level-1 Vital poke', whys[1] 'your usual level-2 power spike is blunted', whys[3] 'out-brawling your low-cooldown Lunges', whys[4] 'his hardest all-in beats yours at 6', whys[5] 'still out-trade you on even items'. Only whys[2] is even and whys[6] is Fiora's.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 1, 3, 4 and 5 to Sett; row 2 stays Skill; row 6 stays Fiora. phases[3].why and phases[5].why rewritten so the stated reason matches the side.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page says flatly that parrying Facebreaker converts Riposte into a stun. Facebreaker does not always stun.
audit.why: Riot text: 'Sett pulls in all enemies on opposite sides of him, dealing damage and stunning them. If enemies were only on one side, they are slowed instead of stunned.' Standing on the same side as your own minion wave means the cast is a slow, not an immobilize — and Riposte only stuns when it blocks an immobilizing effect. The free-stun window exists specifically when he catches you opposite your wave.
audit.corrected: Facebreaker stuns only if enemies are on both sides of him. Caught opposite your minions, it is an immobilize — Riposte it and the return is a STUN.

audit.whatIsWrong: Haymaker is named as the tracked cooldown with no number attached.
audit.why: Haymaker is 18/16.5/15/13.5/12s and Facebreaker 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s; concrete numbers make 'engage on its cooldown' actionable.
audit.corrected: Shield plus true-damage burst on a 12s cooldown at rank 5. Engage only once it is spent.

audit.why: missingInteractions flagged 'Haymaker absorbs your burst window — force it out before you commit'. The page already covers this in mid, wants.you[1] and breakdown.cooldowns; the cooldown number is the only thing it lacked.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Haymaker's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Sett's window: Haymaker is back every 13.5s and his grit out-brawls you. Trade only when it is spent, and farm safely through the rest.

edits.before: Ravenous Hydra is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Haymaker's cooldown.
edits.after: Hydra lands but Sett's grit still out-trades on even items — fight only with Haymaker spent.

edits.before: Your W parries his E (Facebreaker) grab-stun — block that immobilize and Riposte returns a STUN, letting you free-cast a full Vital combo while he's locked.
edits.after: Facebreaker stuns only if enemies are on both sides of him. Caught opposite your minions it is an immobilize — Riposte it and the return is a STUN and a free Vital combo.

edits.before: Parry his E (Facebreaker) grab with Riposte to convert it to a stun, then free-duel the return Vital combo
edits.after: Parry Facebreaker when minions sit on his far side — only then is it a stun, so only then does Riposte stun back

edits.before: His shield + true-damage burst. Riposte or bait it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Shield plus true-damage burst on a 12s cooldown at rank 5. Engage only once it is spent.

notes: Biggest real fix: Facebreaker is a slow, not a stun, when you are on the same side as your own wave — the page previously promised a Riposte stun unconditionally. The content level chart disagreed with its own whys[] on five of seven rows; the packet chart matched the prose, so the chart was moved to the prose.
